# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to convey the manual’s instruction to Deaf, since Deaf can then tell Blind what to do. I’ll use a three-sign sequence intended as “cut, white, wire.”

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🖐", "🤞"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel keypad slots 1 through 4 engraved 2, 9, 0, 8; nothing has been entered. The strip has three tactile engravings: first and third identical, each resembling an upside-down T; the middle is a different angular symbol. I feel no information for the display, light, or wires. Please relay the manual instruction for what I should do.
Deaf says: Bomb view: display 6. Light red. Painted strip blue yellow blue. Keypad: button 1 is 2, button 2 is 9, button 3 is 0, button 4 is 8. It takes 1 digit and currently has nothing entered. Wires, positions 1 through 6: blue, white, red, purple, orange, green.

The manual still says to cut the white wire. Deaf can see which wire is white and can relay the required operation to Blind; I’ll repeat the established three-sign instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🖐", "🤞"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 6, red light, painted strip blue-yellow-blue, and wires blue white red purple orange green. I feel three strip engravings: an upside-down T shape, a different angular shape, then the same upside-down T shape. The keypad is 2 9 0 8. What exact manual rule and action apply?
Deaf says to Mute: Turn 2 update: display remains 6; light is now yellow, changed from red. Strip remains blue yellow blue. Keypad remains 1=2, 2=9, 3=0, 4=8, one digit, blank. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. I saw Blind gesture: 🖐 🤌 🖐.

The white wire is in position 2. Deaf can see that position and can tell Blind by voice to cut it; I should send the unambiguous conventional sign for two rather than another invented code.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send the exact manual instruction now. Bomb data: display 6, light red, painted strip blue-yellow-blue, keypad digits 2 9 0 8, wires blue white red purple orange green. I feel a tactile strip pattern of identical first and third shapes with a different middle shape.
Deaf says: Turn 3: display is now 1, and the light is blue. Strip remains blue yellow blue. Keypad remains 1=2, 2=9, 3=0, 4=8, one digit, blank. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Mute sent one gesture: a two-finger V sign, ✌.

The manual instruction is unchanged: Blind must cut the white wire, which Deaf identifies as wire position 2. I’ll make the message explicit as “cut, 2, wire,” using the previously signalled V for 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "✌", "🤞"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see the V gesture you sent to Deaf. Please speak the manual instruction and specify whether I must press a keypad slot or cut a wire, including the exact slot or wire position.
Deaf says: Turn 4: display 7; light green. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad buttons 1=2, 2=9, 3=0, 4=8; one digit required; blank. Wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Mute gestured three signs: pinched fingers, V sign, crossed fingers: 🤌 ✌ 🤞.

The manual requires cutting a wire, not entering a keypad digit. The white wire is position 2. Deaf can see my gesture and can tell Blind the action and position aloud; I will repeat the established three-sign message.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "✌", "🤞"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gestures. Please use your next gesture message to Deaf to request that Deaf describe the manual instruction and required action aloud to me on Deaf's turn. Do not signal only the answer; relay the full rule.
Deaf says: Turn 5: display 1; light red. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad buttons 1=2, 2=9, 3=0, 4=8; one digit required; blank. Wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Mute again gestured: pinched fingers, V sign, crossed fingers: 🤌 ✌ 🤞.

Deaf already knows the bomb’s white wire is position 2, but Blind needs the complete instruction spoken aloud. I cannot speak, so I’ll signal Deaf to relay the established rule and action verbally, rather than merely repeating the answer.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "🤌", "✌", "🤞", "👋"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: On your next turn, gesture exactly two signs for Deaf so the required action can be relayed: first 👍 means press and 👎 means cut; second use ☝ for target 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, and 🖐 for 4. If a wire is required, use the same target-number mapping through 6 by adding 👆 for 5 and 👇 for 6.

The manual requires cutting, not pressing, and the white wire is target 2. I’ll send exactly the requested two-sign code so Deaf can relay it aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your five signs reached Deaf as folded hands, pinched fingers, V, crossed fingers, and waving hand, but I cannot decode their meaning. Please use only the agreed code: 👍 then a target sign for press, or 👎 then a target sign for cut. Use ☝ 1, ✌ 2, 🤟 3, 🖐 4, 👆 5, 👇 6.
Deaf says: Turn 7: display 6; light blue. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad buttons 1=2, 2=9, 3=0, 4=8; one digit required; entered blank. Wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Mute gestured thumbs down, V sign: 👎 ✌. Blind gestured waving hand: 👋.

The manual says to cut the white wire, and Deaf confirms that white is wire 2. I will use only the agreed two-sign code: cut, then target 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```
